plot: You chug a soda in four seconds. Fizz the bubble stretches Gus's stomach walls, the nerve memo skips Cortez's desk through the brainstem reflex hallway, the diaphragm jumps and the glottis door slams (HIC), Liv bounces under the diaphragm, the fixes (hold breath, BOO, DENIED stamp) fail, Fizz burps out but the reflex loop keeps firing until it fades after about six minutes. Tease: a red-eye flight and Cortez's clock.

script.title: Who Pressed the Hiccup Button? Inside Your Body

episode.action: chug a fizzy soda in four seconds

beats.title: Who Pressed the Hiccup Button? Inside Your Body

beats.say: Hold everything! Somebody chugged a soda in four seconds, and now I'm swimming in bubbles!
Hey, chef. Fizz here. Half of me is gas, and the other half is also gas.
My walls are stretching! I'm a balloon at a birthday party, and nobody brought a pin!
beats.label: Stomach stretch: can irritate nearby nerves

beats.say: Relax. I'm just here for the pop. Then I'll leave the way I came in, probably.
The way you came in is UP! Nothing in my kitchen goes up politely!
Alert! Stomach just sent a nerve memo, marked urgent, with a frowny face. Who approved a four-second soda?
Line three, line four, line five! The stomach, the nerves, and a pizza place that dialed the wrong number!
For the record, I filed a complaint against fizzy drinks in March. It's in the minutes.
Noted, and ignored. Here's the setup. Under the lungs sits a big dome of muscle, and it does most of your breathing.
beats.label: Diaphragm: your main breathing muscle

beats.say: Hi! Hi! We love the diaphragm! It pulls down, we breathe in. It relaxes, we breathe out.
Today, the diaphragm got a message that says: JUMP. Nobody asked me. I'm the manager!
Sending it now! A stretched stomach tickles the nerves that run up to the diaphragm. It's not personal.
Wait. That message isn't coming to my desk. It's taking the reflex hallway through the brainstem, and I'm not on that route.
beats.label: Reflex arc: skips conscious thought

beats.say: So you're not even in the loop?
I'm the manager. I'm never in the loop. Why do you think I drink so much coffee?
Everything is calm. We are inhaling nicely. We are inhal... GULP!
That's it. The diaphragm yanked down, and the door between the vocal cords slammed shut. That slam is the HIC.
beats.label: Glottis: the gap between your vocal cords

beats.say: Rude! We were mid-breath! Nobody knocks on the door like that!
And every single hic bounces me around the chest! I'm a receptionist, not a drum!
Okay, team. Fix number one. In and Out, hold your breath.
No! No way! We're couriers, not statues! We have deliveries!
Fix number two. Beat, jump out from behind the desk and scream BOO.
BOO! ...Is that it? I was told there'd be a bigger reaction.
Nothing. Zero effect. And I wasted a full sheet of paper on the BOO budget.
Fix number three. Distraction. Beat, quick, what's seventeen times twenty-three?
Four hundred and... hic! One? Hic! I lost track, and now I'm embarrassed!
I looked it up. Most folk tricks have little proof behind them. They mostly distract you until the reflex runs out.
Fine. New policy. Hiccups are hereby... denied!
We checked. The diaphragm doesn't read memos. Hic. Sorry, hic.
Nine hics so far. I live right under the diaphragm. It's like having a trampoline park upstairs.
beats.label: Liver: sits right under the diaphragm

beats.say: Every hic, my whole shift bounces. I just spilled a full flask of bile. Again.
Common hiccup triggers include eating too fast, fizzy drinks, alcohol, and sudden excitement.
Or all of the above, at a birthday party. Somebody get me a mop.
I'm the biggest organ in this building, and the diaphragm still wins at bouncing. It's humbling.
A short spell of hiccups is usually harmless, and it ends on its own.
Good news, everyone! I'm leaving! One burp, coming right up!
BURP! And just like that, Fizz is gone. My stomach is back to normal size.
So why are we still hiccing?
Because the reflex doesn't care that Fizz left. The loop keeps firing until the irritation settles.
beats.label: Hiccup spell: reflex repeats, then fades

beats.say: Statistically, most spells fade on their own, in minutes to hours.
Hours?! I have a full calendar! I have a calendar for my calendar!
We'll just keep breathing and ignore the door slamming. We are professionals.
Counting. Twenty-three. Twenty-four. Everything is fine. Stamp it.
Hey, quick update. No more stretching down here. Nothing's poking the nerves anymore.
The reflex is quieting down. Do you hear that? That's nothing. Beautiful nothing.
Is it over? Please say it's over.
We are inhaling. We are exhaling. We are... doing it! No door slam!
Case closed. Total spell: about six minutes. Felt like six weeks.
A spell that lasts more than forty-eight hours is called persistent. That one goes to a real doctor's desk.
Next time: a red-eye flight to New York. Somebody check Cortez's clock.

long.title: Who Pressed the Hiccup Button? Inside Your Body
long.description:
You chugged a soda in four seconds. Gus the stomach swims in bubbles, Cortez finds out the hiccup reflex skips his desk, and In and Out get their breath slammed by a tiny door.
A funny, body-accurate look at why we hiccup: a stretched stomach, the diaphragm, the reflex arc and the glottis.

Real body notes (sources): OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e, The Process of Breathing: https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/22-3-the-process-of-breathing ; NHS, Hiccups: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/hiccups/ ; NCBI Bookshelf, StatPearls: Hiccups (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books).
Entertainment and general education, not medical advice. Original characters, animated in Blender.
